paper_metadata.title: Preparing Arbitrary Continuous Functions in Quantum Registers With Logarithmic Complexity

experiments.description: Adiabatic direct state-preparation of discretized continuous functions using rank-1 Hamiltonian simulation, demonstrated numerically on a log-normal distribution and a Slater-type function across varying qubit counts and iteration counts.

algorithm.variant: Adiabatic rank-1 projector state preparation with low-rank and 1-sparse Hamiltonian simulation

hyperparameters.resolution_qubits_n: varied up to 12 in Fig. 3; general theory uses n qubits
hyperparameters.temporal_discretization_r: varied; plotted over approximately 10^4.5 to 10^6.5 in Fig. 3(c)
hyperparameters.simulation_time_T: constant bounded; selected according to adiabatic condition
hyperparameters.filling_ratio_F: reported for examples; used in theory and tables

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Prepare n-qubit state |psi> proportional to samples f(x_j) on a uniform grid over [a,b], with N=2^n grid points; also considers integral encoding for non-negative functions.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Prepare |psi> = (1/N_norm) sum_j f(x_j)|j> (or g(x_j)|j> for integral encoding) by adiabatically evolving the ground state of H(s) ∝ |psi_s><psi_s|.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: No explicit constraints; uses adiabatic evolution of a rank-1 projector Hamiltonian and post-selection/measurement of ancilla in simulation subroutine.
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: H(s) = -A(s)/N, where A(s) is rank-1 with entries [A(s)]_kl = f_s(x_k) f_s*(x_l) (or N g_s(x_k) g_s(x_l) for integral encoding).

problem_instance.description: Numerical demonstrations on a log-normal probability density and a Slater-type orbital-like function; scalability tested versus qubit count and number of adiabatic iterations.

dataset_specification.description: Continuous functions defined on [0,1]; log-normal and Slater-type examples shown in Fig. 3 and Table I. Log-normal parameters include (mu, sigma) pairs listed above; Slater function uses e^{-alpha|x-0.5|}.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Functions discretized on a uniform grid; function values digitized to d=32 bits in numerical simulations; ancilla reset after each time step.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Exact 1-sparse simulation of the 2n-qubit low-rank embedding; infidelity 1-|<psi|psi_tilde>|^2 plotted versus n and r; empirical scaling fit reported in Fig. 3(c).

quantum_resources.num_qubits: 2n + d + 2 total in the low-rank simulation subroutine; main register n qubits, ancillary register n qubits, plus d-qubit and two 1-qubit ancillas
quantum_resources.circuit_depth: Not explicitly reported; query complexity O(r) and oracle depth depends on arithmetic

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Compute discretized function values; in simulations, round function values to 32-bit precision and simulate the 1-sparse embedding via tensor/Taylor expansion.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Measure ancilla after each step; accept any outcome and reset ancilla to |+>^n; compute infidelity and empirical scaling from simulation outputs.

results.unit: oracle calls per low-rank simulation step

classical_baselines.method_name: classical direct evaluation of N samples

speedup_claims.factor: logarithmic complexity in desired resolution; constant query complexity in n asymptotically
speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical direct evaluation / sampling over N grid points
speedup_claims.conditions: for efficiently computable continuous functions with reasonable filling ratio F and fault-tolerant implementation
speedup_claims.caveats: constant factor depends inverse-polynomially on filling ratio F; pathological narrow functions can make F arbitrarily small

speedup_claims.factor: exponential quantum advantage in query complexity over O(N) classical sampling
speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical evaluation of all N samples
speedup_claims.conditions: when preparing discretized continuous functions with constant asymptotic filling ratio
speedup_claims.caveats: advantage is asymptotic and depends on oracle access and low-rank simulation assumptions

scalability_data.metric_value: approaches a constant in exponential order with n
decreases approximately as O(r^-1.19) to O(r^-1.3)

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Query complexity O(F^p / epsilon^2) for state preparation, with p = -4 for pointwise encoding and p = -2 for integral encoding; per-step Hamiltonian simulation uses 4 oracle queries; asymptotically constant in n for continuous functions after rescaling.
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Classical direct evaluation of N samples would require O(N) queries; direct search example discussed as O(2^(2n)) in pathological case.
complexity_analysis.constant_factor_quantum: Depends inverse-polynomially on filling ratio F; asymptotically constant in n for continuous functions
complexity_analysis.total_operations_quantum: O(r) simulation steps; each step uses constant oracle queries

experiments.description: Phase-estimation-based self-verifying state preparation and normalization-factor estimation for the same rank-1 projector state-preparation framework.

algorithm.variant: Quantum phase estimation on rank-1 projector evolution

hyperparameters.evolution_time_t: chosen so that tN^2/N is in [N/N2^(m-1), N/N^2] per the paper's bounds; selected to make the phase non-zero
hyperparameters.initial_overlap_lambda: must be non-negligible; lower bounded by F^2/(b-a)^2 for the constructed initial state

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Use phase estimation on the unitary generated by the rank-1 projector to recover the normalization constant and/or prepare the target state.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Estimate the non-zero eigenphase of e^{-i tN^2/N |psi><psi|} to infer the normalization factor N and/or project onto |psi>.
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Post-selection on non-zero phase-estimation outcome; repeated sampling until a non-zero result is observed.

problem_instance.description: Generic continuous-function state preparation and normalization estimation; no single fixed dataset beyond the abstract function family.

dataset_specification.description: Applies to arbitrary continuous functions on [a,b]; examples and bounds use the same log-normal/Slater-type functions as the main text.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Prepare an approximate state |tilde psi> with overlap lambda; use controlled powers of U(t) and inverse QFT.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Analytical success-probability and sample-complexity bounds; no hardware experiment reported.

quantum_resources.num_qubits: n + m total in the phase-estimation circuit, plus the n-qubit target register; the paper also references the low-rank simulation subroutine requiring 2n + d + 2 qubits

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Construct initial approximate state |tilde psi>; choose t and m; prepare controlled powers of U(t).
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Inverse QFT and measurement of the first register; infer normalization factor from the measured phase.

classical_baselines.value: not explicitly quantified; described as requiring numerical integration over the grid

speedup_claims.factor: logarithmic / exponential quantum advantage for normalization estimation and phase estimation-based state preparation
speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical numerical integration over the grid
speedup_claims.conditions: assuming fault-tolerant implementation and non-negligible overlap lambda
speedup_claims.caveats: paper gives analytical bounds only; no hardware experiment

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Controlled-U queries scale with m; success probability lower bounded by F^2/(b-a)^2; normalization estimation expected trials O(1/lambda).
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: Classical normalization/integration would require numerical integration over the grid; no explicit asymptotic bound given here beyond the general O(N) sampling discussion.
complexity_analysis.total_operations_quantum: m controlled applications of U(t) plus inverse QFT

experiments.description: Single-ancilla destructive-interference state preparation and verification for continuous functions, including the use of a π-phase projector evolution to amplify the desired component.

hyperparameters.evolution_time_T: pi / ||A/N||_2 for the projector reflection step
hyperparameters.initial_fidelity_lambda: overlap with target state; success probability equals lambda
hyperparameters.number_of_repetitions_r: used in the error bound for repeated projector simulation
hyperparameters.filling_ratio_F: used in the error bound O(F^p / r)

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Apply a controlled reflection e^{-i pi |psi><psi|} to an approximate state |tilde psi> = sqrt(lambda)|psi> + sqrt(1-lambda)|psi_perp> and post-select on ancilla |1>.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Project an approximate state onto the target state |psi> by flipping the sign of the ideal component and interfering it destructively.

problem_instance.description: Generic continuous-function state preparation and verification; no fixed benchmark instance beyond the abstract function family.

dataset_specification.description: Applies to arbitrary continuous functions; the paper illustrates the method using the same function families as the main text.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Start from an approximate state, optionally obtained via adiabatic evolution; use a single ancilla Hadamard-controlled projector reflection.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Analytical success probability and error bounds; no hardware execution reported.

quantum_resources.num_qubits: n + 1 total (n-qubit target register plus one ancilla qubit)

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Prepare an approximate state |tilde psi>; estimate or approximate ||A/N||_2 if needed; set T = pi/||A/N||_2.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Measure ancilla; accept |1> to obtain |psi>; repeat if ancilla outcome is |0>.

classical_baselines.value: not explicitly quantified; failure after m trials is (1-lambda)^m

speedup_claims.factor: single-ancilla verification with polynomially bounded success probability in filling ratio
speedup_claims.conditions: when an approximate state with good overlap is available
speedup_claims.caveats: error bound depends on filling ratio and repeated low-rank simulation; no empirical benchmark

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Repeated projector simulation error O(F^p / r); success probability lambda; one ancilla qubit overhead.
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: No explicit classical comparator beyond general sampling/integration remarks.
complexity_analysis.total_operations_quantum: r repeated low-rank simulation steps plus one ancilla measurement
